encoder: the fleet named in the row id: eight group encoders (G1 to G8) and one integrator, working from the sources alone; the launching session records which models
display_name: Regulation of Engagement in Work on Refrigeration or Air-Conditioning Systems Law, 5785-2025, with its Fees Regulations (draft, as made, as amended): full encoding by a fleet
maintainer: undetermined: to be set by whoever deposits this row
scope: Encoded: sections 1 to 63 and the First, Second, Third and Fourth Schedules of the Law, and regulations 1 to 5 of the Fees Regulations in three vintages (the SimpLEX draft of Figure 4, as made in Kovetz HaTakanot 11951, as amended in Kovetz HaTakanot 12383) with the SimpLEX test table run against all three; an integration layer (int-*.l4) wires the eight groups' modules together and exports five headline functions (the grant of a licence, the right to do work, the sanction for a violation, the commencement dates, the fee for a service). Not encoded: the text of other statutes the Law refers to (their effect is an input), any order or regulation under the Law other than the Fees Regulations (none is in the sources; a rule that needs one returns a named refusal), consumer price index readings, the calendar of days of rest, the opinions and identities of the officials, the Law after Wikisource revision 2947808 and the Fees Regulations after revision 3011135, and the parts of the SimpLEX draft that its screenshot does not show.
not_reviewed: No domain expert has read this encoding against the Law. Every reading is the fleet's, assumed and not ruled, and is marked so in the FRAGMENT that registers it, except one: the owner ruled on 2026-10-14 that day X of s.63(a)(1) is 16 July 2025 (fork F-C-3 of group 7), with the 16 October 2025 alternative documented in NOTES.md. Quotations of the Hebrew were checked by script (srcrefs.py) against the Wikisource text of the Law, the Wikisource consolidated Fees Regulations, and the text layers of Kovetz HaTakanot 11951 and 12383; what the encoders compared against the gazette of the Law (Sefer HaChukim 3349) is recorded in their FRAGMENTs, and nothing beyond that is claimed.

authors.scope: ss.1 to 18, the First and Second Schedules, and the commencement day as they use it
ss.19 to 40, ss.58 to 63 and the Fourth Schedule
Chapter 6 (ss.41 to 57) with the Third Schedule, s.63(b), the Fees Regulations in three vintages and the SimpLEX test table

independent_tests.method: each author decided the expected answer to every scenario from the sources before opening any module of the encoding; the fleet lead audited the authors' transcripts; scenarios written after opening the encoding are labelled probes in the authors' documents and are not counted
independent_tests.note: see the section 'Independent tests' of NOTES.md for the disagreements found and their dispositions
